text: Practitioners must account for optimism bias by making explicit adjustments at the outset of an appraisal.
All data used in an evaluation, regardless of its source, must be collected, transferred, stored, processed and deleted in accordance with GDPR and any specific departmental security processes.
Any common platform you use must have been assured and found to produce outputs that meet the relevant government requirements.
To meet quality assurance requirements, AI systems must be trustworthy, accountable, transparent and robust.
Procurement and contract management must conform with the Government Functional Standard for Commercial.

contains: AI Playbook for the UK Government

text: Organisations shall follow appropriate guidance when implementing data frameworks and operating models, including for cross-government data sharing, business intelligence, artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation and advanced analytics.
Note: The following products provide best practice guidance:
organisations should use the Data and AI Ethics Framework

Evidence that the project has considered emerging technologies (i.e., Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotic Process Automation) and incorporated them into the benefits management approach.
These topics and the examples of evidence should be regarded as indicative and not prescriptive.
The use of AI should be proportionate, quality-assured and verifiable.
The UK government has highlighted general principles and safeguards that should be taken into account for safe and responsible AI usage in the Generative AI framework for HM Government
All central government departments and arm’s length bodies that provide public or frontline services, or routinely interact with the general public, must use the ATRS.
Digital and technology spend controls were replaced on 1 April 2026.
